title: Bilinear base change preserves algebroid colimits
statement: Let $\mathcal V,\mathcal W,\mathcal T$ be cocomplete monoidal infinity categories whose tensors preserve small colimits separately. Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. If $b:\mathcal V\times\mathcal W\to\mathcal T$ is a strong monoidal functor preserving small colimits separately, the bifunctor $(A,B)\mapsto b_*(A\boxtimes B)$ from $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)\times\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal W)$ to $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal T)$ preserves small colimits separately. Here $A\boxtimes B$ has object space $X\times Y$ and mapping objects $(A(x,x'),B(y,y'))$, and $b_*$ composes its enrichment with $b$.

source.place: Corollary 9.2; in the presentable case Corollary 8.17; the proof of Corollary 8.16 uses Segal-presheaf localization in sections 7-8 Read online where available; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-cocomplete-monoidal-tensor] to form $V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W$, with universal strong monoidal $\mu$, and factor $b\simeq\bar b\mu$, where $\bar b$ preserves small colimits. By [lem-coef-algebroid-cocontinuous-base-change], all the algebroid categories in question have small colimits and $\bar b_*$ preserves them. Functoriality of the external product under changes of enrichment in [lem-coef-algebroid-external-product] identifies the bifunctor of the statement with $\bar b_*\,G$, where $G(A,B)=\mu_*(A\boxtimes B)$. We prove separate cocontinuity of $G$ in steps 2-6, without claiming that $b$ or $\mu$ preserves colimits of the cartesian product category.

source.place: Observation 3.9 and reduction to the universal case

proof.text:
For small monoidal $C,D$, the presheaf external product of [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] preserves colimits separately: evaluate at $[n](\boldsymbol c,\boldsymbol d)$, compute the colimit pointwise, and commute that colimit with product by the fixed space in the other factor. These two facts are supplied by [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model]. By [lem-coef-segal-external-local-equivalences], the product takes Segal equivalences to Segal equivalences and takes two Segal objects to a Segal object. The localization unit maps therefore give an equivalence
$$L_{C\times D}(P\boxtimes Q)\simeq L_C(P)\boxtimes L_D(Q):$$
both maps from $P\boxtimes Q$ to these objects are inverted by reflection, and the right-hand object is already local. For a diagram $X:K\to Q_C$ and $Y\in Q_D$, put $P=\operatorname{colim}_K i_CX$ in presheaves. The reflector colimit formula of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] gives
$$(\operatorname{colim}_{Q_C}X)\boxtimes Y\simeq L_{C\times D}(P\boxtimes i_DY)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{Q_{C\times D},k}(X_k\boxtimes Y).$$
For a diagram $Y:K\to Q_D$ and fixed $X\in Q_C$, put $Q=\operatorname{colim}_K i_DY$ in presheaves. The product of $i_CX$ with the unit $Q\to i_DL_DQ$ is a Segal equivalence, and its target is Segal. Pointwise preservation in the second variable and the reflector colimit formula therefore give
$$X\boxtimes\operatorname{colim}_{Q_D}Y\simeq L_{C\times D}(i_CX\boxtimes Q)\simeq L_{C\times D}(\operatorname{colim}_k(i_CX\boxtimes i_DY_k))\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{Q_{C\times D},k}(X\boxtimes Y_k).$$

Now fix monoidally compatible $S,T$ as in [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. Here $Q_C^S,Q_D^T$ use the fixed-endpoint free-edge generators $E_C(S),E_D(T)$, so that locality tests mapping fibres and includes algebroids with empty or disconnected object spaces, by [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model]. Write $R=L_{C\times D}^{S\odot T}$ and $H(X,Y)=R(i_C^SX\boxtimes i_D^TY)$ on $Q_C^S\times Q_D^T$. For a diagram $X:K\to Q_C^S$, set $P=\operatorname{colim}_{Q_C,k}i_C^SX_k$. The unit $P\to i_C^SL_C^SP$ is an $S$-local Segal equivalence. By [lem-coef-segal-external-local-equivalences], tensoring it with $i_D^TY$ is an $S\odot T$-local Segal equivalence. Applying $R$ and then step 2 gives
$$H(\operatorname{colim}X,Y)\simeq R(P\boxtimes i_D^TY)\simeq R\operatorname{colim}_k(i_C^SX_k\boxtimes i_D^TY)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_kH(X_k,Y).$$
The last equality uses that a reflector is a left adjoint; [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] gives both reflector colimit formulas. For a diagram $Y:K\to Q_D^T$, set $Q=\operatorname{colim}_{Q_D,k}i_D^TY_k$ and apply the other-variable clause to $Q\to i_D^TL_D^TQ$; this gives
$$H(X,\operatorname{colim}Y)\simeq R(i_C^SX\boxtimes Q)\simeq R(\operatorname{colim}_{Q_{C\times D},k}(i_C^SX\boxtimes i_D^TY_k))\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{Q_{C\times D}^{S\odot T},k}H(X,Y_k).$$
The first equivalence inverts the product of the displayed unit with $i_C^SX$; the second is step 2 in the second variable, and the third is preservation of colimits by $R$.
The model theorem [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model] supplies the reflective localizations used here.

source.place: Corrected fixed-endpoint version of Corollaries 8.14-8.15; the localization-unit computation works for the hom-fibre-local reflectors.

proof.text: Suppose $V,W$ are presentably monoidal. Choose $V\simeq P^S(C)$ and $W\simeq P^T(D)$ using [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model]. Use that node's corrected equivalences: an algebroid $A$ corresponds to a Segal presheaf $X$ with object space $X([0])=\operatorname{Ob}(A)$ and mapping presheaves $H_X(x,x')=A(x,x')$, each of which is $S$-local. Thus the localization imposes no locality condition on the total edge space without fixing its endpoints. The same node identifies $V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W$ with $P^{S\odot T}(C\times D)$ and $G$ with $H$ of step 3, on coherent diagrams and their canonical maps. For clarity, their object space is the product of the two object spaces, and their mapping presheaves are the coefficient reflection of $H_X(x,x')\boxtimes H_Y(y,y')$; this is precisely the model node's tensor comparison. An equivalence of infinity categories carries a colimit cone to a colimit cone, since its mapping-space equivalences carry $\operatorname{Map}(c,z)\simeq\lim_k\operatorname{Map}(X_k,z)$ to the same universal property. Therefore both canonical colimit comparisons for $G$ are equivalences by step 3. In particular terminal $C$ with $S=\{\varnothing\to *\}$ gives $Q_C^S\simeq\mathrm{Spc}$, retaining the empty and two-point object spaces.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, Lemma 8.3, Observation 8.4, and the hom-fibre correction of Proposition 8.5; Corollary 8.16.

proof.text: For general cocomplete $V,W$, apply [lem-coef-algebroid-universe-embeddings] after choosing the larger universe to contain the coefficient categories and their cocomplete tensor. The repaired node requires no local smallness in the original universe, so its hypotheses follow from those of the item. In a larger universe obtain $J_V,J_W,J_{VW}$, fully faithful and preserving the original small colimits, and a coherent comparison $J_{VW}G\simeq\widehat G(J_V\times J_W)$. The lower bifunctor $\widehat G$ has presentably monoidal coefficient categories, so step 4 applies relative to the larger universe. A diagram small in the original universe is also small there. This does not impose presentability on the original coefficient categories.

Let $A:K\to\operatorname{Algd}(V)$ be small and fix $B$. Using step 5, the image under $J_{VW}$ of the canonical comparison $\operatorname{colim}_kG(A_k,B)\to G(\operatorname{colim}_k A_k,B)$ identifies with
$$\operatorname{colim}_k\widehat G(J_VA_k,J_WB)\longrightarrow\widehat G(\operatorname{colim}_kJ_VA_k,J_WB),$$
which is an equivalence by step 4. The preservation and full faithfulness asserted in [lem-coef-algebroid-universe-embeddings] justify both identifications and reflection of this equivalence. Indeed full faithfulness lifts an inverse and its two inverse identities in mapping spaces. For fixed $A$ and a small diagram $B:K\to\operatorname{Algd}(W)$, the image of the other comparison is $\operatorname{colim}_k\widehat G(J_VA,J_WB_k)\to\widehat G(J_VA,\operatorname{colim}_kJ_WB_k)$, again an equivalence. This proves both comparisons for $G$, including $K=\varnothing$.

Finally [lem-coef-algebroid-cocontinuous-base-change] applies to the genuinely cocontinuous unary functor $\bar b$ from step 1. Consequently
$$b_*((\operatorname{colim}_k A_k)\boxtimes B)\simeq\bar b_*G(\operatorname{colim}_k A_k,B)\simeq\bar b_*\operatorname{colim}_kG(A_k,B)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_k b_*(A_k\boxtimes B).$$
For the second variable use $\bar b_*G(A,\operatorname{colim}_k B_k)\simeq\bar b_*\operatorname{colim}_kG(A,B_k)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_k b_*(A\boxtimes B_k)$. The factorization and naturality in step 1 show these are the canonical comparisons. The empty diagram is allowed throughout, so preservation includes the initial algebroid.
